title: Liam Livingstone criticises England setup, claims ‘no one cares’ about players not in inner circle
content:
Liam Livingstone has launched a scathing attack on the England management, accusing them of a lack of respect, and does not expect to feature for the national team again under the current setup.

The all-rounder, who has made 100 appearances across Tests, one-day internationals and T20s, has not represented England since the Champions Trophy a year ago and was omitted from the white-ball teams last summer, with the national side opting against renewing his central contract in September.

In an interview with ESPNCricinfo, the 32-year-old said he has since had two telephone calls with members of the England management team, neither of which lasting longer than a minute. One was with coach Brendon McCullum, who informed him that he had not been selected for the white-ball series against the West Indies in June as they wanted to look at alternatives in the all-rounder role.

He claimed there was no contact with the outgoing selector Luke Wright, and only a text message from captain Harry Brook. “That probably sums that group up as a collective,” said Livingstone. “Keysy said nothing — (he) said I’ll speak to you in the summer. I actually rang him one day, and he said he was busy at a Test camp at Loughborough. And then I didn’t hear off him until the end of September.

“That was a bit of an eye-opening experience about the group and the regime: if you’re in, you’re in, and if you’re not in, no one cares about you.”

Livingstone, who won the Indian Premier League with Royal Challengers Bengaluru last year and has since been signed by Sunrisers Hyderabad for Rs13 crore (£1.06million; $1.4m), had a brief telephone exchange with Key in September in which he was informed he was losing his central contract.

England insist that Livingstone will still be considered for selection if he performs strongly in domestic and franchise cricket.

While he was still in the fold, it was also made clear to him that scoring runs consistently in the team represented his best chance of cementing a place in the side.

The 2022 T20 World Cup winner, who captained the national team against West Indies only 18 months ago, endured a slump in form while England struggled, losing 10 out of 11 games across a tour of India and the Champions Trophy in Pakistan.

His highest score was only 14, and he took three wickets, as the side lost all three of their games at the tournament.

Livingstone told ESPNCricinfo that the tournament was the worst experience of his career and added that, when he asked England’s coaches for advice, he was told not to worry so much.

“I was asking for help and pretty much all I got was that I care too much and I need to chill out a little bit, and everything will take care of itself,” he said. “It wasn’t the most enjoyable experience for me.”

The all-rounder last month signed a new three-year contract to play T20 cricket for Lancashire and will feature for London Spirit in The Hundred.
